commands.summary: 25/25 unit tests passed covering outward rounding, arithmetic primitives, cancellation, magnitude extremes, and exact rational oracle dot product bounds
151/151 unit tests passed across entire repository without regressions

requirement_evidence.evidence: Implemented Interval and IntervalVector in ecdr/week4/numerics.py with add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/relu/dot_with_constant. Explicit exceptions for inverted, division by zero, negative sqrt, and non-finite endpoints verified by 25 unit tests.

All primitives apply outward directed rounding (round_down/round_up). Vector reduction uses Higham gamma_{n+1} bounds accounting for n products plus scalar bias accumulation instead of arbitrary one-nextafter.
ExactRationalOracle implemented with fractions.Fraction; verified adversarial cancellation (diff=1e-15), magnitude extremes (1e15 + 1e-15), signed zeros, and dot products.
Tested all 3 multiplication sign regimes (positive, negative, zero-crossing), zero scaling, degenerate point intervals, and endpoint inclusion.
Enforced SmallCNN1D dot product lengths (30, 96, 128, 192, 2048) and verified gamma_n bound. Unsupported lengths (n=42) and untested profiles fail closed with UnsupportedNumericalError.
Preserved dyadic float32 weights exactly as real inputs; embedded execution profile and Higham rounding model in primitive outputs.
Zero new external package dependencies introduced; pure standard library + NumPy inside frozen .venv. Results logged in primitive_checks.json.

scientific_dispositions: H05: Outward directed rounding and gamma_n bounds establish the foundational layer for certified whole-domain margin bounds.
H07: Confirms that exact interval accumulation preserves containment, though wrapping effect remains present for deep graphs.
H22: Formalizes the exact discrepancy between real arithmetic and float32 reduction, closing the first gap in the numerical bridge.
limitations: Interval multiplication uses worst-case 4-point bounding; while sound, it does not track dependency between repeated occurrences of identical variables.
